entities.name: "Onboarding" is used for two different things.

attributes.note_text: HR uses "onboarding" to mean *employee* onboarding (PROC-HR-001). Implementation and Customer Success use "onboarding" to mean *customer* onboarding (PROC-IMPL-001). Always disambiguate: "employee onboarding" vs. "customer onboarding." Several older Support tickets and Slack references use bare "onboarding" and must be interpreted from context.

- Sales and Marketing materials predominantly say **"client."** - Customer Success and Support predominantly say **"customer."** - Finance and the billing system use **"account"** or **"customer account"** as the formal record-keeping unit (one account can technically map to multiple tenants/contracts). These are not always perfectly interchangeable — a "client" in a Sales context may refer to a prospective company before a contract exists, whereas "account" in Finance always refers to a billable, contracted entity. There is no single company-wide style guide enforcing one term; this is a long-standing, low-priority inconsistency.
See organization.md, "Note on Titles." Pre-2025-03-01 documents say "Project Lead"; current documents say "Implementation Manager." Same role.

Engineering's SDLC documentation (PROC-ENG-002) uses "defect." Support-facing documentation (PROC-SUP-001) uses "bug." The ticketing system field is literally labeled "Issue Type." All three refer to the same underlying concept: a confirmed deviation from expected product behavior.
